issues.legal_issue: Special leave obtained through deliberate withholding or misrepresentation of material facts may be revoked.
material_facts: A tenant had deposited money in an earlier proceeding but withdrew it before the trial court decided the later eviction suit.

The tenant knew that the money had been withdrawn, but his special leave petition omitted that fact and presented the deposit as available to the landlord, relying on the High Court’s statement that the record did not prove withdrawal.
The Supreme Court granted special leave on the misleading presentation; disclosure of the withdrawal would have affected whether the Court exercised its discretion to grant leave.
issues.conclusion: The Court revoked the special leave and ordered the appellant to pay the respondent’s costs.
issues.legal_principle: The jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution is discretionary, is exercised sparingly, and is not a general appellate jurisdiction. An applicant invoking that discretion must approach the Court candidly and disclose information that may bear on its decision. If the applicant deliberately misleads the Court or withholds material information to obtain leave, the Court may refuse leave or revoke leave already granted, including at the hearing of the appeal. The Court relied on Har Narain v. Badri Das and approved S. B. Shetty v. Phirozeshah Nursservanji Colabawalla.

rule.if: special_leave_proceeding and leave_granted and applicant_knew_material_fact and material_fact_withheld and fact_could_affect_leave_discretion and misleading_presentation

predicates.special_leave_proceeding: The matter is an application or appeal for which the court’s special leave is sought.
predicates.leave_granted: The court granted special leave after considering the applicant’s presentation.
predicates.applicant_knew_material_fact: The applicant knew a fact relevant to the matter when making the presentation to the court.
predicates.material_fact_withheld: The applicant did not disclose that relevant fact to the court.
predicates.fact_could_affect_leave_discretion: The undisclosed fact could have affected the court’s decision whether to grant leave.
predicates.misleading_presentation: The applicant presented the matter in a way that created a materially false impression about the relevant facts.

issues.definition: When a party seeking special leave knowingly withholds a fact that could affect the court’s discretion and presents the matter misleadingly, leave already granted may be revoked.
